operations.comment: ; Readability notes, rounds 1 through 4. Physical offsets include the 16-byte iNES header.
; Effective execution PRG slots [0,1,2,3] underlie the CPU aliases in this listing.
; Unknown intervals remain opaque local incbin slices; no decoding claim follows.
; Scratch04..Scratch0F and StreamPointer are caller-owned temporary storage.
; DrawingX/Y, target bytes, SetupStep/Timer and BoardStep bytes are shared by
; title/setup/transition phases. Names describe their principal consumer, not exclusive ownership.
; Object arrays have six slots; player slots 0..3, auxiliary objects 4..5.
; OAM fields use byte stride 4: Y, tile, attributes, X. X is often the OAM cursor.
; Sound arrays also use byte stride 4; eight records span primary/secondary groups.
; PlayerKind: 0 absent, 1 human, $80 computer. AnsweringPlayer is one-based.
; Controller pressed bits are rising edges; held masks survive until the next poll.
; Mixed data comments distinguish consumer-derived subviews from unknown original grouping.
; Consumer-derived table aliases name the observed access contract, including
; subviews into mixed lookup storage. They do not assert a full table extent.
; Round 2 execution entries and caller-specific scratch views. PRG slots [0,1,2,3].
; Further caller-specific views used by drawing, OAM exchange and feature code.
; iNES metadata: mapper 1, 32 KiB PRG, 32 KiB CHR, no trainer. Not CPU code.
; InitializeGame: Disable interrupts, initialize stack, PPU and APU, then choose the initial screen. MMC1 setup lives in the fixed-bank reset stub.
; InitializeOptionsAndTitle: Initialize sound channels and default setup counts, load palettes and title graphics, and install the title frame handler.
; TitleFrame: Animate the title using fractional position/velocity accumulators. Start/button activity or the title timeout selects the next screen.
; SelectInitialPpuMode: Select PPU control mode 2 for this initialization path, then join the common screen setup.
; TitleTimingAndBounce: Delay to the display split, select title CHR and integrate the fractional bounce. On the lower bound, reflect/damp velocity before testing Start and timeout.
; BlankDisplayAndNametable: Disable rendering before clearing the screen and hiding sprites; callers subsequently write PPU data directly.
; EnterTitleOptions: Build the initial option frame, load palette/text, and install the setup screen frame callback.
; InstallSetupScreenCallback: Install a frame callback supplied in X/Y after setting the screen control flags. Continues through the common dispatcher setup.
; SetupSpriteCoordinateRows: Two four-byte coordinate rows: SetupSpriteXTable then SetupSpriteYTable. Setup sprite construction indexes these in parallel.
; SetupScreenFrame: Process the setup delay and Start transition, draw the four selection sprites, and return to the frame tail.
; RestartInitialScreen: Return to the common initial-screen setup after the preceding option check.
; SetupStartDelayCheck: Wait for the startup sound channel to finish or count down the Start delay, then draw the setup prompt and selection icons.
; EnterPlayerOptions: Initialize player/difficulty selection graphics and counters, then install the option interaction callback.
; FillPpuWithBlankTiles: Write 64 copies of tile $0B to the current PPU destination; requires rendering disabled or a safe PPU update window.
; FillPpuRegion: Set PPU address from A/X, then fill the selected span through the alternating tile writer.
; WriteSetupText: Select the setup text rectangle and send it to the rectangular tile writer.
; WriteSetupTextAtLowAddress: Use A as the low PPU destination byte and X/Y as the source pointer for rectangular setup text.
; SetupCursorAndBracketTables: Setup cursor coordinate rows followed by option-bracket PPU address bytes. Consumers index the named subviews separately; this is mixed lookup storage.
; WriteNineAttributeBytes: Write nine bytes from the setup attribute table at the selected PPU address. Y advances through the table.
; DrawSetupAttributePattern: Draw the fixed selection frame tile/attribute pattern. PPUCTRL changes select the destination stride.

; OptionRowAddressAndTileTables: Tail of the option-row PPU-address table and adjacent tile-base selectors. The high-byte view begins in the preceding accepted data; aliases describe consumer accesses across this boundary.
; DrawOptionBracket: Draw the bracket using horizontal/vertical PPU increments, then restore horizontal increment. X/Y encode the destination.
; PlayerOptionsFrame: Advance option reveal/selection states, read fresh button edges and update human count, computer count and difficulty. Timed states share scratch bytes.
; CommitSetupRendering: Update scrolling/mask and enable the setup PPU control mode, then wait a bounded software delay.
; AdjustOptionCount: Adjust a bounded count in Y from fresh directional button bits. Y=$01..$04 is the supported range.
; SetOptionRowPpuAddress: Use the selected option index in X to load its PPU destination from parallel tables.
; DifficultyValuesAndText: Four difficulty thresholds, four text offsets and encoded difficulty-name records. Text combines destination bytes with seven-bit glyphs and a high-bit final glyph.
; DrawCountSprites: Draw A repeated count markers, advancing the X coordinate by $40 each time; Y supplies the row.
; DrawDifficultyTicks: Convert difficulty into groups of eight ticks and append fixed tile/attribute sprite records to shadow OAM.
; InitializePlayersAndBoard: Build player-kind slots from human and encoded computer counts, initialize positions and board state, then enter board setup. A zero kind terminates the populated slots.
; AdvanceComputerPlayerInitialization: Advance the player slot and decrement the remaining computer count; repeat the PlayerKind=$80 store until X reaches zero.
; TerminatePlayerList: Append empty player slots and initialize each present player's logical square, screen position and sprite kind.
; InitializeBoardScreen: Turn rendering off, select CHR/palettes, build board graphics and shadow OAM, then choose the next board interaction handler.
; EnterBoardScene: Install the board scene callback with the corresponding PPUCTRL mode after preparing the common scene state.
; PrepareBoardSceneTransition: Hide the first sprite, start the transition sound and return the board callback address in X/Y.
; InstallBoardFeatureIntro: Store the category sprite color and install BoardFeatureIntroFrame through the callback helper.

; BoardFeatureStatusFrame: Refresh status text on alternating frames. Every 32 frames write zero to another player/category indicator and queue paired effects; keep the board and auxiliary object moving until SceneCountdown expires.
; ChooseFeatureStatusText: Choose the stage/player message; one stage/difficulty combination emits an extra text fragment.
; WriteFeatureStatusText: Append two selected text fragments, then the current player counter and shared status tiles.
; AdvanceFeatureStatus: Pause the scene countdown while the current player is moving. Four category indicators advance independently of the per-frame board rendering.
; MaybeAdvanceFeatureObject: The preceding call or frame mask leaves A here; values at least 14 with bit zero set trigger another auxiliary update.
; RenderFeatureStatusFrame: Update player sprites, auxiliary slot 4 and board strips, then dispatch the next frame or finish the countdown.
; BoardFeatureIntroFrame: Animate the auxiliary object during the timed feature introduction. ScenePhase selects fade, sound and target-square changes before the shared frame tail.
; RenderFeatureIntroObject: Before phase $A0 draw players in depth order; all phases continue drawing the auxiliary object and applying the board split.
; CheckFeatureIntroMilestones: The A=$68 milestone transfers to feature setup. At phase $B1 clear auxiliary movement and queue an effect; later alternate frames may advance it again.
; MaybeStepFeatureIntro: Only even phases with BoardSceneEffectFlag set advance the auxiliary feature state.
; FinishFeatureIntroFrame: Join the ordinary sound/frame dispatcher.
; FeatureIntroSquareOffsetData: Four auxiliary target-square offsets, indexed by current player in BoardFeatureIntroFrame. Values $3F,$43,$47,$4B are added to the selected category.
; StageTimesSixteen: Return stage selector shifted left four bits; used to form per-stage offsets.
; BeginBoardFeatureResolution: Initialize the feature counter and square class. A different board section shifts the feature state before the common resolution path.
; PrepareFeatureTransitionCallback: Prepare the next board transition callback, then use its returned state to select the common feature resolution.
; ResumeBoardAfterFeature: Restore the board transition timing and callback after a feature-related state. Exact feature route remains a redirect question.
; InstallFeatureStatusFrame: Stop the current player, update object state and install BoardFeatureStatusFrame with a fresh countdown/category index.
; RestoreBoardSceneCallback: Reinstall board timing, PPU control and frame callback after a feature scene; copy transition state before returning to the frame tail.
; ResolveBoardSquareClass: Read the current player's board square and reduce its packed value to the even class-table index in SquareClass.

; ResolveCompletedCategorySet: Sum the four category indicator fields for the current player. A sum of four selects the alternate sound, destination projection and next board stage; otherwise retain the ordinary resolution.
; ReturnBoardClass: Return to the board-class caller. The following lookup storage is separate from this return entry.
; ExtractSquareClass: Shift a packed board value and mask to an even class index. Does not itself validate the board index.
; LoadBoardDestinationPosition: X selects a high/low board projection pair. Return it in BoardPositionHi/Lo without changing X or Y.

; InitialBoardObjectAndAttributeData: Initial object sprite selectors and squares, stage-marker positions, and board attribute section selectors. Parallel named views have distinct index domains; no single record stride applies to this mixed block.
; EnterPuzzleTransition: Select transition CHR/state, initialize a frame countdown and install the puzzle-entry callback.
; InstallPuzzleTransitionCallback: Reset the frame counter and install the puzzle transition callback for the new scene.
; PuzzleTransitionFrame: Animate the nametable/scroll transition, update rectangular tile bands and then initialize puzzle state.
; JumpToBoardSceneTail: Resume the shared board scene continuation.

; DispatchPuzzleTransitionPhase: Select the transition phase from the state value left by the feature-resolution predecessor; early phases clear nametable bands, later phases animate tile/scroll updates.
; SetPuzzleTransitionPalette: Store the selected working color in the background and category-sprite slots before continuing transition setup.
; InitializePuzzleState: Install puzzle frame state, clear drawing/motion scratch, initialize timer and answer buffers, and copy puzzle palette/graphics state.
; WritePpuTileRow: Write A to PPUDATA 32 times, preserving A. Destination stride comes from PPUCTRL.
; BuildPuzzleScreen: Disable PPU rendering, build the puzzle frame, load base graphics, and select the next drawing state.
; SelectPuzzleChr: Select the puzzle CHR bank and install its PPUCTRL shadow before writing the corresponding MMC1 register.
; PuzzleFrame: Update palette, controller edges, pointer sprites and drawing timers; change to answer input when a player buzzes in.
; StartCategorySound: Index the category-specific sound selector and pass it to the sound driver.

; CategoryStatusPaletteData: Category sound selectors, player status PPU destinations, stage/category palette colors and answer color pairs. Consumers use the named byte/interleaved views; color rows are NES palette codes.
; DrawAnswerSlots: Draw the answer-slot row; selected/unknown letter tiles use the supplied marker and blink phase. AnswerLength bounds the slots.
; DrawPuzzleTimerPointer: Draw the puzzle pointer and time indicator into shadow OAM, then hide unused sprites.
; ReadSelectedPlayerButtons: Map a player slot to controller/button mask and exchange controller state where the selected player needs the second controller.
; DrawingFrame: Run drawing, countdown and player buzz-in checks. Computer slots compare scheduled time pairs; human slots use masked controller input.
; FinishDrawingFrame: Render the current frame's pointer/sprites and enter the common frame tail. The board feature and completion paths also share this frame tail.

; ExchangeRemainingOamFields: Exchange the remaining three OAM fields, completing a whole-record swap. Move the right cursor back eight bytes and repeat while left X remains below it, reversing this sprite-record span.
; DrawingFrameTailJump: Tail-jump to the common sound/frame tail. The preceding record swaps reorder the drawing sprites before this frame tail.
; ComputerReactionThresholdData: Four threshold bytes selected by the computer-response policy. These bound reaction timing; exact difficulty-to-playing-strength interpretation remains tentative.
; ExchangeOamByte: Exchange the OAM byte at X with the byte at Y-4 using Scratch04, then advance both cursors. Four calls exchange a complete sprite record.
; FinishExchangeOamByte: Finish the byte exchange by storing the saved left byte at Y-4, then advance both cursors.
; GetPlayerButtonMask: Map player X to a controller index and button mask. The two-human special case selects shared-controller masks. Returns masked fresh presses in A.

; ControllerMaskLookupData: Sixteen mask-like bytes ($00,$FF,$0F,$C0), following the player button-mask table. Full patterns, neighboring boundaries and available consumer aliases were checked; a complete selector/record schema is unresolved.
; DrawDrawingCursor: Add cursor offsets to the drawing position and render the cursor metasprite at the resulting coordinates.
; AnimateTimerBounce: Integrate fractional timer motion; on the vertical bounds reflect/damp velocity and update the visible timer digit selection.
; LoadTimerDigitGraphics: Select the timer digit's graphics slice and copy tile bytes to the metasprite working buffer.
; CopyTimerTileSequence: Copy a strided tile sequence into the timer metasprite working records, stopping at the scratch limit.
; HideRemainingSprites: Fill unused OAM bytes with $F8 from cursor X to the supplied limit, hiding every remaining sprite. X=$00 is treated as exhausted.
; TimerSpriteAndDecimalData: Four blink sprite-kind selectors followed by packed decimal encodings for timer digits 0..25. The timer tile builder indexes the decimal view.
; FinishPuzzleDrawing: Disable rendering/NMI and clear active drawing state before transitioning away from the puzzle. The continuation blanks the palette and returns to board setup.
; BlankPaletteAndResumeSetup: Disable rendering using incoming Y, fill palette shadow with black, upload it, restore the mask and run the software delay with Y=100 before returning to setup.
; RestorePuzzleScroll: Set puzzle scroll positions and restore PPU state after the software delay.
; InstallFrameCallbackDefault: Select default PPUCTRL, install callback X/Y, reset frame counters and clear hardware scroll/mask before yielding.
; InstallFrameCallback: Store PPU control A and callback X/Y, reset frame counters and disable rendering until the next frame dispatch.
; WaitForFrameDispatch: Wait for NMI-driven dispatch; control is resumed by the callback rather than an ordinary subroutine return.
; WaitVblankFlag: Poll PPUSTATUS until vblank. Reading PPUSTATUS clears its flag/latch; callers use this with NMI disabled or during setup.
; PollControllers: Latch both controllers, shift eight serial bits and compute newly pressed edges against the previous held masks.
; ClearRamPreservingSignature: Compare the four-byte RAM signature, clear working pages, and preserve or initialize the signature page as appropriate. Stack page is intentionally excluded.
; RamSignatureBytes: Four-byte initialization signature copied to RamSignature and compared on later setup. These are persistent-state validation bytes, not executable instructions.
; SetPalettePpuAddress: Set the PPU destination to $3F00 and return Y=0 for the following palette writer.
; WriteFadedPalette: Subtract the fade offset from palette colors, clamp underflow to black and preserve the special mirrored entry rule.
; WriteAlternatePalette: Select the alternate palette destination, then upload the remaining entries with the fade clamp.
; WriteRemainingAlternatePalette: Upload the remaining palette shadow entries. Entries 17..31 subtract PaletteFadeOffset and clamp underflow to black; earlier entries pass through.
; WritePalette: Copy 32 palette shadow bytes to PPUDATA, starting at $3F00.
; DrawPuzzleFrame: Clear nametable tile area, draw borders and per-player status fields, then initialize answer/status rows.
; DrawAnswerAlphabetRow: Write the contiguous alphabet tile row and finish with the blank cell at the current puzzle destination.
; PlayerIconTilePairData: Interleaved icon tile pairs, read through PlayerIconTilePairs0/1 while building the player display.
; WriteAlternatingTiles: Write A then Y repeatedly, X pairs total, to PPUDATA. X must be nonzero on entry.
; WriteAlternatingTilesLoop: Shared interior of the alternating-tile writer; X is the remaining pair count.
; WriteControllerIcon: Copy four icon tiles then skip to the next status field with PPUDATA reads.
; ControllerIconTileData: Controller icon tile selectors in repeated four-byte patterns, indexed by setup/controller state. Exact original grouping beyond the consumer views is not asserted.
; SkipPpuCells: Read PPUDATA Y times to advance the PPU address without overwriting cells. Y must be nonzero.
; LoadDrawingRecordTarget: Read the record X/Y pair through StreamPointer; add eight to X and advance the drawing stream pointer by one coordinate pair.
; SetDrawingCommandState: Set drawing-command state and continue into the command dispatcher; command meaning beyond the established state is tentative.
; ApproachDrawingTarget: Move each integer coordinate by up to three toward its target, snap when close, then advance the command state when both match.
; ScanDrawingAnswerSpacing: A zero byte ends this record. Otherwise advance target X by one tile and skip space bytes; negative Scratch04 transfers to the delayed drawing path.
; DrawingCommandAdvanceTail: Tail-jump to the drawing-stream advancement handler. No new stream format is established here.
; EnterDelayedDrawingTarget: Enter the shared delayed target setup.
; EndDrawingAnswerRecord: Advance the command state at the record terminator.
; DrawingAudioWait: Hold the drawing countdown until the active sound channel completes, then decrement the state countdown.
; NormalizeDrawingDelays: Reduce each nonzero drawing delay/pause to one before continuing the ordinary drawing update.
; UpdateDrawingMotion: Dispatch timed drawing commands, update signed fractional velocities/positions and detect arrival at the target tile cell.
; ReadDrawingMotionCoordinate: Reload the shared computed motion coordinate for the following drawing test.
; DrawingDelayExpired: Count down the current command's remaining delay and initialize the next segment at zero.
; BeginDrawingRecord: Save the current tile, clear command delay and inspect record flags. The second flag byte controls stepping and delayed coordinate setup; $BF retains its bit-1 flag.
; TestDrawingRecordDelayFlag: Save the second record byte bit 1. If set, advance the stream and enter delayed target setup; otherwise return.
; DelayDrawingTarget: Set command state $80, pause 18 ticks and load the next target coordinate pair.
; DrawingExitTarget: Set the target coordinates for the drawing exit motion and decrease its state countdown.
; AdvanceDrawingStreamPair: Advance the drawing command pointer by two, carrying into its high byte.
; InitializeDrawingSegment: Load offsets and velocity parameters for the selected drawing command, combine its base coordinates, and initialize segment state.
; PrepareDrawingCellUpdate: Save cursor/cell state and arrange the next tile update. The direction tables and tile-neighborhood helper define the subsequent coordinate and replacement steps.
; SelectDrawingCommandTile: Use the command-index permutation XOR Scratch08 to select a tile mapping; save both the current and comparison tile.
; DrawingCommandPermutationData: Sixteen command selectors in even-then-odd order. SelectDrawingCommandTile indexes this permutation, XORs a caller flag and then reads DrawingTileMap.
; DrawingCellTargetSetup: Clear cursor offsets, load the tile-cell target and force coordinate alignment bits before PrepareDrawingMotionTarget.
; AlignDrawingCoordinatePair: Finish OR-$03 alignment of the four cursor/target coordinates, then disable the command index and comparison tile with $FF sentinels.
; ClearDrawingMotionState: Clear the drawing accumulator/state buffers before a new motion segment.
; FinishClearDrawingVelocityBytes: Finish clearing all six integer/fractional drawing velocity bytes, then prepare the motion target from the record.

; PrepareDrawingMotionTarget: Mask record and cursor coordinates to tile boundaries. Select a direction class unless the record requests the fixed mode, then combine per-direction flags and offsets to compute cursor-relative X/Y targets.

; DrawingDirectionMotionTables: Interleaved direction flags and signed velocity/acceleration/cursor-offset rows. Direction class selects the paired X/Y entries; motion uses separate integer/fractional bytes. Named consumer views establish accesses, not one universal record size.

; ClassifyDrawingDirection: Compare signed horizontal and vertical displacement magnitudes, distinguishing horizontal, vertical, diagonal and approximately 2:1 slopes. Map the resulting quadrant/slope selector to a direction class in X.
; DrawingDirectionClassData: Fourteen direction-class selectors used by ClassifyDrawingDirection after quadrant and slope tests; values remap geometric classes to the motion-table order.
; TransformDrawingCoordinate: Apply the drawing orientation transform when the orientation flag is nonzero. A holds the coordinate; exact artistic orientation remains tentative.
; IncrementDrawingStreamPointer: Increment the 16-bit drawing stream pointer with carry into its high byte, preserving A/X/Y. Independently supported routine; natural caller not established.
; PuzzleUseBitMaskData: Eight masks $80,$40,...,$01, indexed by puzzle bit position. A selected category uses these to test/set the per-puzzle used bit.

; SelectAndDecodePuzzle: Use category/difficulty selectors and persistent used-bit flags to choose a puzzle without immediate reuse. Fetch a pointer from CHR/PRG storage into a 120-byte decode buffer, then decode coordinates and answer text.
; AdvancePuzzleUsedBitSearch: Advance the candidate bit index and compare against the category used-bit boundary; repeat until a nonmatching slot is found.
; RecordPuzzleUse: Increment the chosen category's puzzle-use count and search for a new unused puzzle bit using mixed random state.
; AdvancePrgPuzzleCopy: Copy exactly 120 bytes from the selected PRG puzzle payload into PackedPuzzleBuffer.
; DecodeSelectedPuzzle: Choose an orientation mask, decode the packed puzzle and compute coordinate bounds/centering before translating answer characters.

; WriteDrawingRecordTiles: Skip the record coordinate pair, then use each byte high bit as the end marker. Space consumes a PPU read; other bytes count a drawing record and write the placeholder tile $B8.
; AdvanceDrawingRecordTileMarker: Advance Y and shift the saved marker until its high bit ends this record.
; DrawingRecordCoordinateTest: Read and transform the next drawing coordinate when nonzero; the adjoining record handler scans flagged coordinate/answer groups.
; StoreOrientedDrawingCoordinate: For nonzero DrawingOrientation subtract 16 before storing the coordinate. A nonzero stored value begins another record.
; ExtractPuzzleAnswer: Translate the high-bit-terminated answer text into answer tile codes, compute a drawing-length-dependent timer value and finalize the puzzle state.
; FinalizePuzzleInitialization: Initialize answer-input state, cursor timing and initial unknown-letter markers after the puzzle stream is decoded.
; ClearAnswerEntry: Walk the decoded answer and fill entered-letter slots with the unknown marker through AnswerLength.

; PuzzleCategoryCatalogData: Sixteen category counts sum to 503. Used-bit offsets, pointer-storage partition thresholds, category text offsets/orientation masks and high-bit-terminated category names follow. Partitions 93/112/114 select CHR payload banks; the remaining 184 puzzles use PRG storage.
; ExpandDrawingBounds: Read a coordinate from the decoded drawing buffer, mask low flag bits and widen the min/max pair indexed by X.
; SetPpuFromStreamCoordinate: Decode a stream coordinate through the pixel-to-nametable converter and select that PPU destination.
; CenterDrawingAxis: Derive a centering displacement from the min/max bounds. One category bypasses the offset adjustment.

; DrawingOrientationAndTileMapData: Two sixteen-byte mapping rows. The first row has no complete established consumer schema; DrawingTileMap begins sixteen bytes later and selects drawing tiles. Consumers and full low-valued patterns were inspected; no wider domain is implied.
; DrawBoardPlayerIndicators: Draw the configured player indicator rectangles at their fixed board destinations.
; CheckFourthPlayerIndicator: Only draw the fourth player indicator when its player-kind field is nonzero; prepare the PPU destination for the shared writer.
; DrawPlayerIndicatorPair: Draw two rows of player tiles at adjacent nametable rows; preserve the destination in scratch while advancing the player index.
; PlayerIndicatorCountData: Five indicator count/mask values selected by the player indicator writer; zero and shifted $20/$40/$60 values control the number/layout of tiles.
; WritePlayerIndicatorTiles: Combine indicator fields and row offset to choose paired tile codes; advances Y through two rows of packed fields.
; PlayerIndicatorTilePairData: Interleaved indicator tile pairs, selected through the two named consumer offsets.
; WriteBoardHeadings: Write the fixed board headings using raw and rectangular tile writers.

; BoardSectionPointerAndDestinationData: Five little-endian source pointers followed by five high/low PPU destination pairs. Source and destination views are indexed with a two-byte stride by the board section writer.
; DrawBoardSection: Choose a board section's tile source and PPU address, draw its rectangle, and copy 40 attribute bytes for that section.
; DrawCurrentBoardLayout: Resolve the current player's square class, draw current and optional stage sections, then update each populated player's board sprite.
; DrawBoardPlayers: Initialize board sprite state and visit all four player slots, skipping absent entries.

; WriteSetupRectangleTwice: Call the setup once, then return into that same setup for a second write. Each pass reads the literal width 131 and height 132 at $A2FE, consuming source $A2FE..$E68B. The first pass leaves X=0 and A from PPUDATA, so the second destination is $00xx, not the original coordinates. The second RTS returns to the original caller. Requires ordinary caller stack, fixed PRG banks [0,1,2,3], a high-byte-ready PPUADDR latch and no interference with scratch/PPU state. Natural caller and original purpose remain unknown.

; WriteSetupAttributeRectangle: Incoming X/A supply destination PPU high/low. Load the SetupAttributes source pointer and tail-call the bounded rectangle writer. The preceding alternate entry calls this setup and then falls through for a second pass. The literal header is 131 by 132; this mechanical name does not establish an attribute-only destination or layout purpose.
; ReadRectangleHeader: Read width and height from the stream at X/Y, keep the pointer in scratch and derive the row skip to a 32-cell nametable stride.
; WriteTileRectangle: Select destination low byte A, read width/height header at X/Y and stream rows to PPUDATA, skipping the unused row cells through reads. Source pointer carries across pages.

; WriteTileRectangleBody: Shared rectangular writer entry after the destination low byte is already selected. Width/height are literal nonzero byte counts, not masked dimensions. Row skip is ((width-1) XOR $1F); with setup width 131 this is 157 reads per row. Each setup pass performs 17292 writes and 20724 reads, leaves X=0 and returns A from the buffered PPUDATA read. Source carry keeps the complete setup range in fixed PRG.
; Tile/layout and lookup storage. Rectangle writers consume width/height-prefixed
; tile rows; other setup/player lookup aliases point inside this range. Whole-range
; non-code evidence is stronger than any individual table extent, so keep the
; remaining bytes generic and do not impose an unproven schema.

; ClearBothNametables: Clear the second nametable, then the first, using zero tiles. The call targets $A3A7; its return resumes the $A3A2 high-byte setup and falls through to the same body. Rendering must be disabled by the caller.
; ClearPrimaryNametable: Select the primary nametable and clear its 1024 bytes.
; ClearNametableAtSelectedHigh: Select destination low byte zero and write four groups of 256 zero bytes to PPUDATA.
; HideAllSprites: Initialize X=0 and hide sprite entries by filling shadow OAM with $F8.
; HideAllSpritesBody: Fill the shadow OAM page with the hidden coordinate value. Shared entry keeps the caller's initial X.
; ClearAndDmaSprites: Hide all sprites, reset OAM address, wait for vblank and DMA shadow OAM page $02.
; UploadOamAfterVblank: Set OAM address from X, wait for vblank and transfer shadow OAM page 2.
; AnswerEntryFrame: Render answer slots, hints and countdown, handle human/computer selection, animate letter entry and decide success/timeout. The selected player is one-based in AnsweringPlayer.
; AdvanceHintRow: Move the hint cursor down a 32-cell row and branch to the shared continuation unless it wraps.
; WriteAnswerHintText: Select the hint text stream, index it by the current hint and write one encoded block.
; SkipEmptyHintCell: A zero result skips to the common hint continuation.
; DrawAnswerHintCells: Visit four active hint cells and update their tiles, then write two decimal timer digits and refresh palette/controller state.
; AdvanceAnswerCursor: Move to the next answer position and save its cursor index.
; ComputerAnswerResume: Jump back into answer rendering after the computer's letter-selection fragment.
; KeepSelectedAnswerCursor: On a nonzero result preserve the selected cursor through the shared store.
; InitializeFlyingLetter: Save the pending answer letter, copy its metasprite template, compute its target answer cell and initialize auxiliary object motion.
; IncrementSelectedAnswerCursor: Alternate entry advances incoming Y before storing the selected answer cursor. Static entry contract; no observed caller is claimed.
; StoreSelectedAnswerCursor: Store the selected answer position; the preceding alternate entry increments incoming Y first.
; AdvanceFlyingLetter: Check the letter object's vertical state and call the common bounce/motion helper until it settles.
; SetAnswerComparisonSeed: Seed A with one for the following answer comparison path.
; CommitFlyingLetterMotionFlag: Store the updated letter movement flag and continue the shared answer animation path.

; CompareEnteredAnswerLetter: Convert the entered glyph to the stored answer encoding and XOR the expected letter. Advance past a blank answer position. A mismatch launches the letter object, starts a hint delay and queues an effect; a match selects the success effect.
; HandleAnswerLetterComparison: A zero comparison selects success. Otherwise place the letter sprite offscreen and initialize its height/movement before resuming answer scanning.
; QueueCorrectLetterEffect: Select the correct-letter effect and join the shared queue path.
; DrawAnswerSelection: Read the current entered-letter slot, render timer/selection sprites, update hints and countdown, and transition when time or answer state ends.

; ComputerWrongLetterChoiceTail: Three trailing wrong-letter choice bytes. The consumer view begins one byte earlier; these choices influence computer answer substitution without defining an independent code entry.
; DrawAnswerTimerIcon: Render the timer icon at its fixed X coordinate and current bouncing Y position.
; FinishAnswerEntry: Reset counters and transfer to the fixed-bank completion hook. The fixed-bank hook installs AnswerCompletionFrame, which evaluates feedback and player replay.
; Isolated $10 conflicts with the neighboring supported instruction boundary. No independent data format or execution contract resolves it.
; Unknown; Unresolved; physical 9991..9992
; InstallAnswerCompletionState: Set the completion callback high byte and delay counter, then yield through the common frame tail. The low byte was supplied by its supported predecessor.
; UpdateAnswerHints: Maintain four transient hint sprites. Avoid duplicate cells, allocate the rotating free slot, decrement lifetimes and draw each active slot.
; HintSpriteVerticalPhases: Five Y-phase selectors $CD,$CC,$CB,$CC,$CD, forming the hint sprite bounce pattern.
; SetPlayerStatusPpuAddress: Use one-based answering player to select that player's status destination from the pointer table.
; DrawAnswerStatusAndPalette: Write status tiles and use alternating frame phases to choose the current two-color palette pair.
; CycleAnswerMarkerPalette: Use the even frame phase to choose an answer palette pair for the blinking marker.
; WriteFourBlankAnswerTiles: Write four $0B tiles at the current PPU cursor; callers establish address and increment mode.
; ClearCompletionNametableBands: Clear three 32-byte bands beginning at PPU $2300 and fill the last 16 attribute bytes at $23F0 with $55.

; AnswerCompletionFrame: Completion callback installed by the fixed-bank hook. ComputerAnswerFlag bit 0 selects the active drawing/fade path; the other path evaluates the answer, displays feedback and chooses replay or transition.
; UploadCompletionOam: Upload shadow OAM when this countdown is not the nametable-clear milestone.
; AdvanceCompletionDrawing: Restore PPU mode, update the drawing and answer state, then periodically raise selected palette entries toward category colors.
; RaiseCompletionPaletteEntry: Clamp nonblack entries upward to the selected category color; traverse palette entries 27..24 and 3..1.
; ChooseCompletionTransition: A short remaining countdown initializes scene transition state and object updates; longer countdowns retain completion rendering.
; FinishCompletionDrawingFrame: Use the shared completion renderer.
; RestartAfterCompletionDelay: Return to the common setup/restart entry after the delay expires.
; EvaluateCompletionAnswer: Upload OAM and service any post-answer delay. At frame $24 compare nonblank stored answer letters minus one with entered letters, then choose the feedback text.
; CheckCompletionFrameMilestones: Frame $24 tests answer correctness; later $FE starts the feedback/remaining-player sequence.
; CompareCompletionAnswerLoop: Ignore zero answer bytes; all others must equal the entered glyph after subtracting one.
; SelectIncorrectAnswerFeedback: Select the alternate feedback text and increment the completion result state.
; WriteCompletionFeedback: Write the selected PPU text record, then restore normal completion display state.
; CheckCompletionReplayTime: Before frame $FE continue palette upload. At $FE initialize the next feedback phase; afterward search for a present player who has not answered.
; FindNextAnsweringPlayer: Scan four player slots, skipping present players already marked answered. Exhaustion displays the no-player text and starts a $C0-frame delay.
; DelayAfterAllPlayersAnswered: Show the final message, initialize the delay and clear the answer display.
; CheckPlayerAlreadyAnswered: Skip an answered player; otherwise restore the answer-entry callback and its timing state.
; ResumeAnswerEntryForNextPlayer: Prepare the next answer attempt, install its callback, extend the puzzle timer and reinitialize answer/display state.
; UploadCompletionPalette: Upload the current faded palette before common display setup.
; RestoreCompletionPpuMode: Restore control mode and scroll state before drawing completion sprites.
; SetCompletionOamLimit: Select cursor $24 before hiding the unused completion sprites.
; FinishCompletionOam: Hide unused OAM from cursor $24 up to $60. Frame $25 initializes the category state and result-dependent sound once; late countdowns also draw the answer marker.
; StartCompletionResultSound: Start the selected sound and latch bit 1 in the completion state so this result is recorded.
; DrawLateCompletionMarker: Draw the answer marker only for countdowns at least $21, then enter the common frame tail.

; StageChrSelectionData: Five CHR bank selectors. StageChrSelectorsMinusOne addresses the first byte for a one-based caller; StageChrSelectors addresses the next byte for its zero-based view. Values are mapper register inputs, not effective physical PRG bank indices.
; ClearAnswerCompletionDisplay: Write the answer attribute/tile blanks, select the second destination and advance 28 PPU cells and clear the corresponding tile group.
; SetScrollAndPpuControl: Write PPUCTRL and the first scroll byte, then send Y through the common scroll/mask writer.
; SetScrollFromY: Use Y as the second scroll coordinate after clearing the first coordinate; apply the shadow render mask.
; SelectStageChrAndPoll: Choose the stage's CHR selector and poll controllers after the mapper write.
; PollControllersReturn: Return through the shared controller polling routine.

; DrawBoardObject: Project an object's logical position into screen coordinates, clip offscreen objects and append its metasprite. Object X/Y arrays include six slots, with special handling for slots 4 and 5.

; BoardProjectionParameterPairs: Four high/low board projection parameter pairs indexed by category. The first byte previously failed an attempted KIL code interpretation; the actual indexed consumer establishes non-code data. CategoryParameters elsewhere is a different table.
; GetCategoryParameter: Return the parameter selected by category; exact parameter meaning depends on the caller.
; DrawCurrentPlayerStatus: Choose the current player's status text and dispatch the encoded text writer.
; IncrementCategoryPaletteIndex: Advance the caller-owned palette selector in Scratch04 and return.
; UpdateBoardScenePpu: Update board scene tiles/palette and use timed scene callbacks to select the status overlays. Delay loops synchronize the split-screen update.
; JumpToStatusTileWriter: Continue with the common status tile writer.
; RefreshBoardFade: Refresh the faded palette and continue through board-scene PPU updates.
; SelectFirstStatusText: Select text offset zero before the alternate-page board text writer.
; BoardFeatureDelay: Choose a short software delay for the feature timer state, then proceed to shared board drawing.
; SelectAlternateStatusText: Select text offset 17, write the selected record and resume at the second palette/status group.
; UpdateCurrentPlayerCounter: Refresh the current player's counter and conditionally draw category/player text according to animation phase and feature flags.
; WriteAlternateStatusMessage: Write the selected fixed text fragment and two adjacent status fragments before the common finish.
; WriteCategoryAndPlayerOverlays: Choose text offsets for category and player status and emit the corresponding overlay blocks.
; WriteTimerStatusText: Choose the player-dependent text, append a timer-digit-selected record and suffix, then add a marker tile unless TimerDigit equals one.
; CommitBoardScenePpu: Draw player indicators, select the scene control mode and CHR banks, delay for the split and restore PPUCTRL.
; SetSceneAnimationGroup: Keep the low animation phase nibble and replace the high bits with $C0.
; BoardSceneFrame: Update board scene/player state, feature counters and movement, then draw, scroll and dispatch sound through the common tail.
; ReadCurrentSquareFeatureClass: If the prior test is zero skip to shared feature logic; otherwise read the current player square feature flags.
; ClearBoardFeatureTimer: Clear the feature timer and continue with the ordinary board path.
; AdvanceBoardFeatureTimer: Work on every fourth phase only. Decrement the feature timer, raise player height slowly in phases $D0..$EF, then select the alternating late-phase behavior.
; ContinueBoardScene: Resume shared board rendering after the feature timer/animation path; the precise game rule selecting the feature remains uncertain.
; SetBoardFeatureLatePhase: Set scene phase $A8 before continuing the feature animation.
; FinishBoardTimerPhase: When the phase matches and sound is idle, resolve the board square class before continuing.
; StartBoardFeatureSound: Start the previously selected sequence, then continue feature logic.
; AdvancePlayerTargetSquare: Increment the current player's target square, wrapping it by the stage-specific count/offset tables.
; SelectBoardFeatureEffect: Start sequence $12 and load the selected feature parameter from the adjacent board lookup.
; StoreBoardCategory: Store the selected category and continue the active feature state machine for the current player.
; ContinueBoardFeatureWhenActive: A nonzero result joins the common feature continuation.
; TestBoardFeaturePhase: Save feature flags and branch on scene phases to update the player's height or logical square.
; MoveToPreviousBoardStage: Set upward height velocity, decrement feature flags and stage, reload the stage destination projection and disable display before restart.
; ShiftFeatureSquareBack: On the matching feature phase, subtract one board row ($10) from the current player's logical square.
; SetFeatureObjectTarget: Save the selected square and initialize object height to $C0.
; RenderBoardSceneObjects: Call each selected per-player helper indirectly, draw the stage marker, render players in depth order and update feature/effect timing. Start enters the pause/restart path.
; AdvancePlayerFeatureCounter: Increment the current player's per-slot feature counter. The following carry helper normalizes the encoded counter tiles.

; CarryPlayerCounterDigit: Normalize the low digit when its XOR-$0A result is $F0, carry into the high digit and clamp a terminal $FA high digit to $F9 in both positions. The counter uses encoded tile values, not binary arithmetic.
; WriteRawPpuTable: Read the PPU destination/count header, then copy literal bytes from the fixed table to PPUDATA.
; WriteRunLengthPpuTable: Read destination/count, then expand value/count pairs into PPUDATA. Zero remaining output count ends the command.
; ReadTileRun: Read the next value/count pair and advance X twice. The caller expands the count.

; BoardPpuRunAndAttributeData: Mixed board tile-run pairs (tile value, run length), raw tile lookups and attribute bytes. The run consumer expands each selected pair to PPUDATA; adjacent named tables have separate formats and bounds.
; DrawPlayersInDepthOrder: Copy player-kind occupancy into a temporary list, repeatedly choose the greatest projected depth and render it, then draw the auxiliary object when appropriate.
; DrawPlayerWithSceneFlags: Choose sprite visibility/attribute flags from scene state, then draw one player and its fixed status marker.
; DrawFixedPlayerMarker: Draw a player's marker at its table-selected screen coordinate; skip absent players.
; ApplyBoardSplitScreen: Wait for the sprite-zero hit, delay to the split point and switch PPU/CHR rendering state. This uses a polling timing scheme rather than a raster IRQ.
; DrawFeatureMarker: Project the current player's auxiliary marker and append its metasprite when the relevant scene state permits.

; BoardRowSelectorData: Four lookup bytes between bounded board routines. Full byte patterns, adjacent instruction endpoints and available consumer views were checked; precise row/selector semantics remain unresolved.
; PaletteFadeSceneTick: Darken the sprite palette on selected scene phases, then update the common fade divider/countdown.
; AdvancePaletteFade: Advance a three-step divider, countdown and palette darkening. Returns a nonzero value while the fade can continue.
; DarkenFullPalette: Select all 32 colors for the shared saturating darken loop.
; DarkenPaletteRange: Subtract $10 from X palette colors beginning at Y, clamp underflow to $0F and skip the mirrored background entry.
; AdjustBoardScrollCoordinate: Compute the scroll-derived board coordinate with signed direction handling and wrap around the $F0 vertical range.
; ComputeBoardStripPpuAddress: Convert the adjusted board scroll coordinate into the next nametable strip destination, saving its high/low bytes.
; SetBoardAttributePpuAddress: Convert the board scroll coordinate to its attribute-table row address.

; BoardStripSourceDescriptorData: Board row counts, source indices, widths, source pointers and destination offsets. Consumers select a descriptor and stream rows into the board-strip buffer; named views overlap the mixed descriptor storage.
; UploadBoardStrip: Read and preserve neighboring attribute nibbles, upload a 32-tile board strip, then merge its attribute bytes.
; BuildBoardStrip: Clear the strip buffer, select the board section from projected scroll position and copy its appropriate source row into the buffer.
; GetAttributeLowNibble: Read a board attribute-table byte and return its low nibble.
; GetAttributeHighNibble: Read a board attribute-table byte and return its high nibble.
; ExtractBoardStripHighNibble: Shift the packed strip selector down four bits for the shared decoder.
; MergeBoardAttributeNibble: Merge the newly computed board attribute nibble with the preserved neighboring nibble and write eight bytes.
; AdvanceBoardScroll: Advance the board scroll position by the current step, update the logical position and wrap the vertical coordinate over $F0.
; BoardMovementFrame: Upload newly exposed strips, move toward the selected board destination with a bounded step, animate active features and return through the frame tail.
; FinishBoardPlayerMove: Store movement state, recompute the object, clear height, decrement feature state and reset the timer digit.
; BoardArrivalFrameTail: Draw the stage marker, delay, and yield through the common frame tail after board arrival.
; JumpToBoardStripContinuation: Join the shared board strip continuation.
; UpdateFeaturePlayerHeight: Update player height while the feature is active, using a bounded rise until the scene can continue.
; AnimateBoardTransitionJitter: Resolve the board strip destination before continuing its row transfer.
; RenderMovingBoardPlayers: Advance scrolling, draw four players and an optional feature marker, then hide the unused OAM tail and rebuild the next board strip.
; DecrementBoardStripDelay: Count down the transition delay; nonnegative values repeat the preceding strip work.
; RestoreBoardTransitionChr: Choose the transition CHR page and run feature effects before entering the common sound frame tail.
; HideBoardStripTransitionSprites: Hide unused OAM up to byte offset $74 using the existing cursor X.
; BoardSoundFrameTail: Update the sound driver and continue at the PPUCTRL restore portion of the frame tail.
; AnimatePlayerHorizontalJitter: Periodically subtract or add one from the selected player's X coordinate to create a small alternating jitter.

; BoardProjectionAndPlayerMarkerData: High/low destination projection pairs followed by player sprite kinds and ordinary/winner marker offsets and coordinates. Different consumers select their own view and stride.
; DrawStageMarker: Choose a stage marker's fixed coordinate and write its tile, attributes and position into the first OAM record.
; RestoreScreenScroll: Clear the first scroll coordinate, write the second and apply the shadow PPU mask.
; WriteSecondScrollAndMask: Write A as the second scroll coordinate and apply PpuMaskShadow to PPUMASK.

; SoundSequencePayloads: Command streams reached through the 19 four-channel sequence pointer sets. Three-byte stream headers lead to high-bit note selectors, durations and positive command/operand bytes; repeated motifs and substream pointers occupy this whole payload area. Individual stream extents and a universal token grammar remain unresolved. The MMC1 register address alias that happens to fall inside this physical storage is not an audio label.
; CycleWinnerTile: Cycle the winner decoration tile index from one through three.

; BuildWinnerScreen: Disable rendering, draw the WINNER scene, load the selected player/color palette and install its animation callback. Entry was exercised artificially with an inspected state contract.
; WinnerPaletteOffsetData: Four palette offsets selected by the winner layout routine; each chooses the corresponding player palette view.
; DrawWinnerDecorationTile: Choose the winner frame's edge tile from the row band and write it to PPUDATA.
; WinnerFrame: Animate the winner's vertical entrance, palette cycling and four status markers; held buttons can return to startup after the delay.
; WinnerMarkersAndSoundPeriods: Winner X/Y marker coordinate rows followed by 19 sound sequence tick periods. Tick-period selector and four-channel pointer-set selector share the same sequence index.
; StartSoundSequence: Resolve the sequence selector into four channel stream pointers, initialize channel state and decode each first command.
; QueueSecondarySound: Queue a sound effect in the secondary channel group unless it already matches the active selector.
; QueueEffectAtChannelFive: Select queue offset $14 and enter the shared sound-effect queue writer.

; QueueEffectAtChannelSix: Select queue offset $18 and enter the same queue writer; SoundScratch supplies the effect selector. This sibling entry has a static contract, without an observed caller claim.
; QueueLastSecondarySound: Use the final secondary channel slot for the shared queue operation.
; InitializeSoundInstrument: Resolve an instrument selector, load its register defaults and initialize the channel stream pointer.
; InitializeSoundCommand: Initialize envelope/register state from the stream header, then save the first command pointer.
; UpdateSoundModulation: Update channel modulation before writing APU output. Independent vibrato, pitch and volume timers share the four-byte channel stride.
; JumpToSoundPitchOscillation: Join the shared envelope/timer update.
; AdvanceSoundModulationTick: Decrement the channel modulation timer. The adjoining reload handler applies a signed delta to the channel timer.

; UpdateSoundModulationDelay: A nonzero preceding test skips modulation. Otherwise reload the modulation tick, count down its active duration, choose the signed delta and add it to the 16-bit channel timer.
; UsePositiveSoundModulationDelta: Use the stored pitch delta directly once the direction-delay counter expires.
; AddSignedSoundModulationDelta: Sign-extend A through SoundPointerHi and add it to the low/high timer pair.
; UpdateSoundPitchOscillation: Apply signed pitch increments on the oscillator timer, reverse direction after its half-period and retain fractional register bytes.
; UpdateSoundVolumeEnvelope: Advance the channel envelope according to its delay, speed and target volume. Disable the envelope once the target low nibble is reached.
; ReloadSoundEnvelopeCycle: On the zero path restore the envelope count, invert the decremented target volume and rejoin the shared output stage.
; ApproachSoundTargetVolume: Raise or lower the channel volume toward its target low nibble; clear envelope mode when it matches.
; WriteSoundChannelRegisters: Write timer low and control/volume to the indexed APU channel. Only write timer high when changed, avoiding unnecessary length-counter reloads.
; AdvanceSoundChannel: Continue the channel tick path and dispatch command data when the duration expires.
; ReadSoundStream: Load the current channel's stream pointer and interpret notes or command opcodes. Positive command bytes dispatch through a handler table.
; DecodeSoundNote: Convert the note selector to an APU timer using the note table. Channel-group flags select alternate register handling.
; ReadNextSoundDuration: Advance the stream cursor, read the following duration and enter the shared duration/pointer store.
; ReadSoundDuration: Choose fixed or stream-supplied duration and save the advanced channel stream pointer.

; UpdateSoundDriver: Advance the sound tick divider and visit channel records in four-byte strides. Process queued sounds, durations, notes and command dispatch; update APU registers through indexed channel addresses.
; ReadSoundNoteOrCommand: Read the next stream byte; zero stops the channel, high-bit values select notes and positive bytes dispatch commands.
; SaveAdvancedSoundStreamPointer: Add stream offset Y to the channel pointer with carry, then save the advanced low/high bytes.
; NextSoundChannel: Advance X by four to the next sound channel record, stopping at $20.
; ReturnSoundTick: Return after all eight channel records have been visited.
; StopSoundChannel: Clear the channel activity byte and silence its APU control register before visiting the next channel.
; SoundCommandClearAlternateFlag: Clear channel active bit 0, advance the stream cursor and resume note parsing.

; DispatchSoundCommand: Multiply the command index by two, resolve its handler through the command table and tail-jump to it. The eighteen-entry handler table includes note, pointer, register preset, modulation and envelope commands.

; SoundCommandHandlerPointers: Eighteen little-endian handler pointers. Dispatch doubles the positive command index and loads low/high bytes from the two aliases. The final word ends before SoundCommandSkipSavedPointerByte; this table does not prove every command occurs naturally.
; SoundCommandSkipSavedPointerByte: Advance Y once and enter the shared stream-pointer-save path.

; SoundCommandApplyRegisterPreset: Read a preset byte offset from the stream and copy four consecutive bytes to the channel shadow and APU registers. Restore the stream cursor and read the following duration before saving the stream pointer.

; SoundRegisterPresetData: Four four-byte APU register presets in control/sweep/timer-low/timer-high order. The command operand is a byte offset into this block, rather than an implicitly multiplied preset number.
; SoundCommandVariableDuration: Select stream-supplied note durations and resume decoding.
; SoundCommandFixedDuration: Read the fixed duration byte from the stream and resume decoding.
; SoundCommandRegisters: Load control/volume, sweep and timer-high defaults from three stream bytes.
; SoundCommandJump: Read a little-endian stream destination and continue there; Y resets to zero.
; SoundCommandCallLoop: Save the repeat count and return pointer, then jump to the command substream. A single stored return slot constrains nesting.
; SoundCommandRepeatReturn: Decrement repeat count; return to the saved pointer when finished, otherwise revisit the stored repeat destination.
; SoundCommandPitchOscillation: Read oscillation extent, tick interval and signed pitch delta, then resume stream decoding.
; SoundCommandDisablePitchMotion: Clear the pitch period, consume the command and resume stream processing.
; SoundCommandPositiveModulation: Read the five-operand modulation setup and retain its pitch delta as supplied.
; SoundCommandNegativeModulation: Read the same setup and negate the pitch delta with two-complement arithmetic.
; FinishSoundModulationSetup: Save the signed delta and following direction-delay byte, then continue parsing.
; ReadSoundModulationSetup: Read delay, period-minus-one, duration and delta operands in stream order. Store period+1 in both reload/current ticks and return with Y at the delta operand.
; SoundCommandDisableEnvelope: Disable automatic volume envelope and load the immediate low control/volume bits.
; SoundCommandEnvelope: Read envelope delay, rate and target volume and resume stream decoding.
; FinishSoundEnvelopeCommand: Reload current channel volume before the shared envelope register update.
; SoundCommandSetEnvelopeCycle: Select envelope mode 2, load delay and half-delay count, period+1 and target volume, then enter the shared envelope-command finish.
; SoundCommandDisableEnvelopeCycle: Clear envelope mode, advance the stream and resume processing.

; SoundTimersInstrumentsAndSequencePointers: Decreasing note timer words, instrument pointers/templates and 19 sets of four little-endian channel stream pointers. Note and instrument consumers use their named views; sequence start multiplies the sequence index by eight. The mixed block has no single shared stride.

; PrepareComputerResponses: Use difficulty and pseudo-random state to schedule computer player reactions. The policy searches category/square state and derives difficulty-scaled randomized delays; exact playing-strength intent remains tentative.

; ChooseComputerResponsePolicy: Combine difficulty with pseudo-random state. Either choose a short random reaction or search uncompleted categories and nearby board squares to derive a response delay.
; FindComputerTargetCategory: Probe four category indicators beginning at a randomized category for this player; avoid the active category and completed indicators.
; FindNearbyComputerTargetSquare: Preserve the player board section and search backward within its 16-square ring for the chosen category. Difficulty chooses a four/five-square starting reach.
; SearchComputerSquareRing: Compare the square category, decrement estimated distance and wrap the low nibble without changing the board section.
; StoreComputerReactionTiming: Store the derived delay and a difficulty-scaled randomized second timing byte in the selected player pair.
; NextComputerPlayer: Advance the computer-response player loop and return after all four slots. The policy choices and timing stores are explained at their branch entries.
; WriteAlternateBoardTextSelection: Select text stream base $CD03 and enter the shared text writer. Y is the record offset; this is an alternate text page, not a three-byte record length.
; WriteBoardTextSelection: Set text stream base $CC02 and dispatch the encoded record at offset Y; the alternate entry selects base $CD03.

; BoardStatusTextAndOffsets: Encoded PPU text records and offset selectors. Each text record carries destination high/low then seven-bit glyph bytes, with bit 7 marking the last glyph. Category/player status consumers choose offsets into these records; the block is not a uniform fixed-size string table.
; SelectMetasprite: Resolve the metasprite pointer from A, preserve the Y coordinate and combine encoded mirror flags with caller sprite attributes.
; DrawBlinkingMetasprite: Select a metasprite and derive a frame-dependent attribute bit before entering the common renderer.

; MetaspriteAdjacentLookupData: Eight patterned bytes beside the metasprite renderer. Available references, neighboring code boundaries and full bytes were checked; no independent complete format or selector domain is established.

; DrawMetasprite: Append a zero-terminated stream of tile/X-offset/Y-offset/attribute records to shadow OAM. X is the OAM byte cursor; SpriteX/Y give the anchor. Supports reflected X and scene-dependent horizontal spread.
; DrawMetaspriteRecords: Read each metasprite tile until zero, project position offsets, XOR attributes and advance the OAM cursor by four.

; MetaspritePointersAndTemplates: Metasprite pointers, offsets, tile/attribute records, answer-letter and timer templates, digit sequences and initial board sprites. The renderer consumes zero-terminated tile lists and per-tile placement/attribute fields; neighboring lookup rows retain their consumer-specific formats. Not every byte is a four-byte record.
; ReturnAuxiliaryEffect: Return from the auxiliary-effect path; the adjacent stage and positioning lookups remain separate data.
; UpdateAuxiliarySceneEffect: Integrate fractional effect motion and select phase-dependent sprite positions. The game-specific effect identity remains uncertain.

; DrawAuxiliaryEffectSegment: For the last segment add a triangular vertical offset from phase Y; otherwise use the base Y. Clip nonzero high-coordinate results, emit one OAM record and advance the phase and seven-pixel base spacing.
; UseFlatAuxiliarySegment: All but the selected last segment have no triangular displacement.
; AddAuxiliarySegmentBaseY: Add the segment displacement and feature counter to the base Y; a nonzero high result clips this OAM segment.
; AdvanceAuxiliaryEffectSegment: Advance the phase by two modulo 64, move the segment base by seven pixels and repeat for the remaining segments.
; CallIndirectScratch: Tail-call the routine in the scratch pointer. A pointer value alone does not establish classification of the target.

; StageSquareCountAndWrapData: Interleaved per-stage square count and wrap-offset values plus neighboring low-valued lookup bytes. Stage arithmetic reads the named views with its stage-dependent stride; exact meaning of trailing values remains unresolved.
; TogglePlayerIndicatorField: Toggle a per-player/category indicator bit selected by category and current player.
; ReturnAuxiliaryObjectStep: Return from the auxiliary object step.
; UpdateBoardFeatureObject: Update the feature object's direction, sound/effect data and scene-dependent sprite selector. Feature activation prerequisites remain unresolved.
; SetPlayerCategoryIndicator: Set the selected PlayerIndicatorField0 byte to one and return.
; UpdateFeatureSoundAndAnimation: Adjust feature sound pitch/template bytes, queue the secondary sound, and select the auxiliary object's animation state from the current scene phase.
; UpdateFeatureSoundAndAnimationEntry: Inspect auxiliary movement and feature flags before changing sound pitch/template and animation state.
; SetAuxiliaryTargetSquare: Store the target square/moving state and prepare auxiliary object positioning before copying the player square.
; CopyPlayerSquareToAuxiliary: Copy the current player square to the auxiliary object before common positioning.
; SelectAuxiliarySpriteKind: Choose the auxiliary object's sprite kind from frame phase, transition state and whether it is moving.
; UpdateObjectBeforeMotion: Run the shared object-motion helper, then return.
; UpdateObjectMotion: Compare current/target squares, prepare a new movement vector if needed, integrate positions, and clear motion state on exact arrival.
; IntegrateObjectPosition: Integrate the selected object's fractional X/Y velocity; update its logical square when the target coordinates match.
; IntegrateObjectPositionBody: Shared interior of object integration after the target lookup has started.
; UpdateObjectVerticalBounce: Apply scene-dependent vertical acceleration, integrate height and fractional position, and settle the object when its unsigned coordinate crosses the floor bound.
; ReverseObjectHeightMotion: Initialize height to one and derive half of the negated high height velocity for the shared adjustment path.
; SettleObjectHeight: Clear height and vertical velocity when the object settles, then return.
; DecayObjectHeightWhenNegative: Incoming N decides whether to return immediately. On the negative path decrement a nonzero object height; preserve zero and share the preceding routine return.

; BoardSquareCoordinatesAndOffsets: Interleaved X/Y board-square pixel pairs and neighboring object placement offsets. LoadBoardSquarePixelPair doubles the square index; other positioning consumers use their own offsets. The preceding countdown routine is separate code.
; AdjustStackedPlayerOffsets: Visit players sharing a logical square and adjust their separation offsets before changing the selected object's square.
; InitializeStackedObjectHeight: Initialize height 12, move Y down 12 pixels and derive high height velocity from the separation field divided by eight plus two.
; FinishPlayerSeparationScan: Advance through the four player slots and commit the selected object's new logical square after separation adjustment.
; PrepareAuxiliaryObject: Set up the auxiliary object using shared position/motion machinery. The following height setup and coordinate-pair lookup complete the mechanical entry path.
; LoadBoardSquarePixelPair: Double the square selector to read interleaved X/Y pixel coordinates; Scratch06 receives X and A receives Y.
; SetObjectMovementVector: Clear accumulators, derive signed X/Y differences from the target and scale them by the movement mode. Separate players sharing a square using a table-selected offset.
; ShiftObjectVelocityX: Shift the low/high X velocity pair left once.
; ScaleObjectVelocityX: Shift the signed horizontal delta into a fractional velocity with carries propagated through the high byte.
; ShiftObjectVelocityY: Shift the low/high Y velocity pair left once.
; ScaleObjectVelocityY: Shift the signed vertical delta into a fractional velocity with carries propagated through the high byte.
; FinishShiftObjectVelocities: Finish the X high-byte carry, then double the Y pair and return.
; InitializeObjectVerticalBounce: Select the initial vertical velocity for player versus auxiliary objects and clear height/fraction before returning.
; PlayerSeparationOffsetData: Seven separation offsets used to spread players sharing a square. Lookup values adjust projected placement without changing logical square identity.
; LoadPalettePair: Wait for vblank and load the selected palette halves into both the palette shadow and PPUDATA. X/Y supply table indices; palette mode selects any alternate path.
; LoadPaletteColors: Shared palette loading loop; selects an alternate source when palette mode is nonzero.

; OrdinaryAndWinnerPaletteData: NES palette codes in repeated four-byte color groups. LoadPalettePair selects ordinary/winner subviews into palette shadow and PPUDATA. The mixed palette set spans 152 bytes; bank selection and scene choose its use.

; EnterPauseOrRestart: Disable display and APU, suppress NMI and change the CHR/palette mode for the pause/restart path. The continuation builds a pause display, polls fresh controller edges and restores its saved sprite-zero Y.

; BuildPauseScreenSprites: Load the pause palette and build five rows of eight OAM tiles. Hide sprite zero while waiting for a fresh controller press, then restore audio, rendering state and the saved sprite-zero Y.
; BuildPauseTileRow: Emit eight OAM records across the row. After the upper four rows, move to the lower row and change its attribute bit.
; BuildPauseTileCell: Write position, table tile and attributes at OAM cursor X; each cell advances X by four and screen X by eight.
; AdvancePauseTileRow: Keep the next row Y, stop after forty tiles and wait in the input loop.
; WaitForPauseControllerPress: Wait for vblank, upload OAM, enable rendering and poll fresh button edges. A press restores state and returns to the frame dispatcher.

; PauseAndAuxiliarySpriteData: Repeated metasprite/tile/attribute patterns following the pause input loop. Full patterns, neighboring endpoints and metasprite consumers were inspected; precise grouping of every auxiliary list remains unresolved.
; ConvertCurrentDrawingPixel: Load current drawing coordinates and fall through to pixel-to-nametable conversion.
; PixelToNametableAddress: Convert pixel X/Y into nametable address: tile X is X/8, tile Y is Y/8, and high Y bits select the nametable page.
; SetDrawingPpuAddress: Copy the computed nametable high/low pair to PPUADDR.

; UpdateDrawingTile: Use drawing state and pixel-to-tile address to update drawing graphics. The neighborhood helper preserves matching joins and can emit temporary motion sprites; exact artistic intent of each command remains uncertain.

; UpdateDrawingCellFromPpu: Discard the buffered PPU read, then inspect the tile. Blank/$B8 cells are cleared; other tiles can emit a temporary sprite before the cell is rewritten. Update drawing delay/dirty state afterward.
; ClearDrawingPlaceholderCell: Restore the PPU cursor and write incoming Y for blank/placeholder tiles.
; FinishDrawingCellReadback: Clear the tile-state latch. A newly dirty cell inherits DrawingRecordCount as its command delay.
; NormalizeDrawingCommandState: Convert the flagged command state to its active form and update the drawing cell through the shared address converter.
; WriteDrawingLetterAtPreviousCell: Move the PPU cursor back one cell and write DrawingLetterTile only when nonzero.
; DrawingDelayOrCellUpdate: Skip the cell update while command delay is nonzero; otherwise load the drawing coordinates and convert them to a PPU address.

; UpdateDrawingTileNeighborhood: Direction class selects PPU increment, coordinate masks, table row and tile transforms. Read three neighboring tiles, preserve compatible joins and rewrite the affected cells; restore vertical increment mode on return.
; IndexDrawingTileRow: Transform the masked Y coordinate, optionally double it, then combine the X contribution to select the tile-operation record.
; ResolveDrawingTileOperation: The operation byte supplies a transform index plus flags: bit 6 backs up the PPU cursor, bit 5 permits additional neighbor writes.
; ReadDrawingNeighborTiles: Read the three buffered PPU neighbor tiles, restore the cursor and choose between preserving a special join or transforming the first tile.
; TransformFirstDrawingNeighbor: Transform the first tile unless the middle tile already matches the special current-tile join.
; MaybeTransformRemainingNeighbors: Operation bit 5 enables the second tile; command classes 6/11 also inspect delay and current-tile equality before choosing the third.
; RestoreDrawingPpuIncrement: Restore PPU control $82 and return to drawing.

; TransformDrawingNeighborTile: Choose the replacement from the transform table. Blank, placeholder and already-correct tiles skip sprite emission; a changed real tile may become a temporary sprite before replacement.

; EmitDrawingTileMotionSprite: Align the caller coordinates to a tile cell. Suppress duplicates using a three-cell circular history; otherwise emit an OAM tile and advance the bounded drawing sprite cursor.
; CheckSecondDrawingHistoryCell: Compare the candidate with history slot one before checking the third.
; CheckThirdDrawingHistoryCell: Compare the candidate with history slot two; a match suppresses duplicate sprite emission.
; RememberDrawingMotionCell: Write the new X/Y pair into the three-slot ring and wrap its cursor at three.
; WriteDrawingMotionOam: Emit the original tile with attributes $22. Cursor $FC is saturated rather than wrapping beyond OAM.
; RestoreDrawingTransformIndex: Restore the caller X and load the replacement tile for the shared PPU write.
; WriteDrawingReplacementTile: Write replacement A to PPUDATA, then advance the transform index and drawing coordinate by eight.
; AdvanceDrawingTransformIndex: Advance table index X and choose the ordinary eight-pixel drawing step.
; AdvanceDrawingTransformCoordinate: Incoming A is a signed pixel step. Command low bits select Scratch08 (X) or Scratch09 (Y).
; AdvanceDrawingTransformY: Advance the Y scratch coordinate by the selected signed step.

; DrawingNeighborhoodLookupData: Direction-indexed PPU control/step, coordinate masks/XOR, tile row thresholds and offsets, replacement tiles and operation records. UpdateDrawingTileNeighborhood uses operation low five bits for a transform index; bits 5/6 request extra neighbor writes or cursor backup. Named tables retain their separate byte-index domains.
; WritePlayerCounter: Select a player's counter destination, choose ordinary or winner layout and write its two counter bytes plus the trailing marker.
; WritePlayerCounterOrdinary: Write the ordinary player counter location, preserving the winner-specific alternate entry.

; PlayerCounterDestinationData: Four high bytes, four ordinary low bytes and four winner low bytes for player counter PPU destinations. The two writer entries select the ordinary/winner low-byte view.
; WriteTextBlocks: Set stream pointer X/Y and block count A, then decode the requested number of text blocks.

; WriteTextBlocksFromPointer: For each block read PPU address high/low, translate 7-bit character indices through the glyph table and end the block at a high-bit-set character. Pointer advances across pages.
; WriteTextBlockLowAddress: Shared text interpreter continuation at the destination low byte.
; Screen/text/tile records consumed near the encoded text writer. Text blocks
; contain a PPU destination and high-bit-terminated glyph indices; mixed nearby
; tile data prevents declaring one uniform format across this entire range.
; EnableRenderingShadow: Set background/sprite enable bits in the render-mask shadow; hardware mask is committed elsewhere.
; ReadAttributeDestinationHeader: Select attribute table $23C0 and initialize a 64-byte output budget.
; WriteCompressedRectangle: Read a rectangular header and expand run commands. A high run bit selects ascending tile codes; otherwise repeat the same tile. Skip unused cells at row boundaries.

; This prefix mixes scratch access and flag-locking branches. The closed PPUMASK suffix has an independent contract, but does not establish a complete entry contract or data schema for these 25 bytes.
; Unknown; Unresolved; physical 24161..24186

; TogglePpuMaskForever: Alternate PPUMASK between $18 and $99 forever. Initial A=$99 and EOR #$81 keep Z clear; STA preserves Z, so BNE always returns to the toggle. The original purpose and caller remain unknown.
; Isolated RTS after a terminal loop has no established entry; instruction-like storage alone does not establish code.
; Unknown; Unresolved; physical 24195..24196
; ChooseCategoryPermutation: Initialize the category permutation array and select 16 unique values from the category transform table using pseudo-random state.
; TryCategoryPermutationValue: Transform a random nibble according to the current category group and reject values already in the permutation array.

; CategoryPermutationTransformData: Twenty-four category transformation bytes selected by the category permutation logic. Low-valued repeated patterns and consumers establish lookup storage; exact distribution/intended permutations remain uncertain.

; NmiFrameDispatcher: Reset the stack and disable rendering/NMI, optionally DMA shadow OAM, increment frame counters and jump through FrameCallback. This is a frame scheduler, so ordinary interrupted execution is discarded.
; IrqReturn: Return from IRQ; no mapper raster IRQ service is implemented here.
; FrameTailWithSound: Update sound channels, restore the PPUCTRL shadow, mix pseudo-random state and wait for the next NMI dispatch.
; FrameTailRestoreControl: Restore PPUCTRL before entering the common random-update/wait tail.

; MixRandomState: Mix four state bytes with controller/frame/setup bytes using carry-sensitive rotates, addition, subtraction and XOR. This is game pseudo-random state, not a stable external RNG contract.

; DecodePuzzleBitstream: Decode the 120-byte puzzle buffer into packed coordinate/flag records. Commands encode absolute coordinates, relative direction steps, flags and a trailing answer string; stream bit position is retained across reads.
; ContinuePackedPuzzleCommand: A nonzero command flag selects the alternate packed command decoder.
; DecodeRelativeDrawingSteps: Use the low command nibble as a direction index; repeatedly add the signed X/Y deltas and emit coordinate records while reducing the packed step count.
; DecodePackedCoordinatePairs: Advance the packed input, save bit position, and append nonzero coordinate pairs to DecodedDrawingRecords. Zero returns to the shared command dispatch.
; DecodePackedCommandContinuation: Handle the special packed command/bit-position case, advance the stream as required and continue into the packed coordinate/answer paths.

; DecodePackedAnswerBlock: Read a signed repetition count and optional bit-position mode. Append flagged coordinate and answer records; each packed letter has a five-bit value plus spacing in its upper three bits. Mark the final record and append a zero terminator.
; BeginPackedAnswerRecord: Set previous-record flag bit 1, append the next two coordinates and advance packed input after each.
; DecodePackedAnswerGlyph: Keep the spacing bits from one byte and the five-bit glyph from the next, storing glyph|$40 in the output.
; ExpandPackedAnswerSpaces: Subtract spacing units of $20; intermediate units append literal space tiles before the next glyph.
; FinishPackedAnswerRecord: Mark previous output with bit 7 and repeat while the signed count is nonnegative; finally append zero.
; DecodePackedAnswer: Extract packed five-bit answer characters into the decoded record stream. Mark the last coordinate record and preserve stream bit position.
; ReadPackedFiveBits: Extract a five-bit field at the current bit position from two bytes, advance the byte pointer when crossing eight bits and preserve the destination index X.
; AdvancePackedStreamByte: Advance the packed stream pointer by one byte with page carry.
; PackedDrawingDirectionDeltas: Two sixteen-byte signed direction-delta rows: X then Y. The packed decoder masks the command to four bits and adds the selected deltas to its current coordinate pair.

; PrgPackedPuzzleRecords: 184 packed puzzle records selected through the CHR-resident high-first pointer catalog. PRG pointers are offsets from CPU $E0FD. The decoder expands coordinate commands, relative direction steps and packed answer fields into RAM. Independent static decoding consumes exactly the next catalog start for all 184 records, ending at physical $7F62 before the fixed hook. This copy path reads 120 bytes into PackedPuzzleBuffer; consumed record lengths vary. CHR storage also contains catalog/puzzle bytes, so CHR is not exclusively artwork.
; FinishAnswerFixedHook: Store answer completion state, install the completion callback low byte and continue through the answer state setup.
; Uniform $FF non-code run before the fixed-bank delay/MMC1 helpers. No semantic
; payload or natural consumer is established; preserve as generic storage.
; DelayXY: Busy-wait using nested X/Y countdowns; timing depends on entry counts and NTSC instruction execution.
; ResetMmc1Serial: Write bit 7 to MMC1 to reset its serial write latch.
; WriteMmc1Control: Send A to MMC1 control, least significant bit first, in five writes. A is shifted and destroyed; register values are not effective physical PRG bank indices.
; WriteMmc1ChrBank0: Send five bits of A to MMC1 CHR bank register 0. Effective mapping depends on the current MMC1 control mode.
; WriteMmc1ChrBank1: Send five bits of A to MMC1 CHR bank register 1, destroying A.
; WriteMmc1PrgBank: Send five bits of A to MMC1 PRG bank register, destroying A. Callers must re-establish effective PRG slot context before assuming aliases.
; ResetEntry: Reset the MMC1 serial state and program control/CHR/PRG registers, then jump to main initialization. This ROM's observed effective PRG slots are [0,1,2,3].
; ResetVectorPaddingBytes: Two $FF bytes between the reset jump and interrupt vectors. Uniform bounded storage; no particular original padding intent is asserted.
; CPU vectors: little-endian NMI, reset and IRQ entry addresses; aliases refer to the fixed upper PRG window.
; CHR cartridge storage: four 8 KiB banks, containing NES pattern tiles and packed puzzle/catalog data.
; MMC1 CHR selection controls PPU-visible storage. Puzzle selection reads a 503-entry high-first pointer catalog at PPU $0C00 and fetches CHR/PRG payloads; this is not exclusively artwork.
